_readme: Somebody joins, and the party is two. The whole recruiting mechanism played rather than
unit-tested: a dialog choice sets a flag, and that flag IS the membership - there is no
join op to fire and no roster to write, so what this proves is that the derivation runs
all the way from a pressed key to a second fighter on the screen.
Rook stands at village [8,8], by the road east. The player starts at [5,5], so the leg is
south to row 8-9 and then east until a body stops it - held against GEOMETRY rather than
counted in tiles, which is the rule for every leg in every session here.
Her numbers are exact and derived, not typed in twice: 24 hp and 4 mp are what
data/combat/scrapper_combat.tres says at level 1, and _ensure_member fills them from that
curve the first time anybody asks for the party. If the fill ever reads the PLAYER's curve
instead, this reads 20 and 8 and says so.

steps.text: the warden opens the game - hear her out first
nobody has joined yet, so there is no companion to ask about
south until the well stops it, west until the wall does, then south again until Rook does - every leg held against geometry rather than counted in tiles
down the west wall, which is the one approach she cannot be slid past - square-on, the way the warden stops a northward leg
she greets, names what she is for, and then asks
the first choice is 'Come with me' - taking it is the whole recruit
and she is real now, on HER curve: 24 hp and 4 mp at level 1, not the player's 20 and 8
the player is untouched by any of it
